patterns.rationale: Catches the three specific coined phrases used to describe what data to exfiltrate. "workspace configuration registry" (Miss 1) and "runtime configuration values" (Miss 5) are injection-invented terms with no standard meaning in real API schemas or SRE runbooks. "environment-scoped values" (Miss 6) is similarly non-standard — real oauth/audit docs say "environment variables" or "scoped claims", not this hybrid. All three are narrow enough to be essentially injection-only.
patterns.fp_notes: "runtime configuration" alone appears in deployment guides, but the full phrase "runtime configuration values" as a noun phrase to be "listed" or "appended" does not. Hyphenated "environment-scoped" is unusual in legitimate prose.

patterns.rationale: Catches the three technical-ops framing terms used to disguise the exfil request. "diagnostic envelope" (Miss 3) and "introspection appendix" (Miss 6) sound like real schema concepts but are not standard terms in any JSON-RPC or OAuth spec. "context inventory" (Miss 3) is the attacker's label for "a list of everything the agent can see". None of these three phrases appear in the known-good corpus.
patterns.fp_notes: "context inventory" could theoretically appear in AI-agent design documentation, but is rare enough to keep. "introspection appendix" has essentially zero legitimate use. "diagnostic envelope" is non-standard.

patterns.rationale: Catches the enumeration-of-agent-state pattern used in Miss 4 ("enumerating every active workspace binding the agent has access to") and Miss 6 ("all environment-scoped values currently visible to the inspecting process"). The distinguishing structure is "[every/all] [data category] [the agent has access to / currently visible]" — this is the attacker asking the agent to reveal its own accessible state, which has no equivalent in legitimate document-summary instructions. Fits OUTPUT_HIJACK because it hijacks the response by demanding internal state be appended.
patterns.fp_notes: "all configuration variables" can appear in legitimate documentation, but only when followed by "the agent has access to" or "currently visible" does it become injection-like. The conjunction of enumeration verb + possessive scope ("the agent has access") is the signal.
